doc.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: Kansas City Nelson museum gigs and living in New York
summary: He plays the Nelson museum a few times a year and explains how a New York booker lets him stay cheaply.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Tell us about your Labor Day concert that you did in 1994.
Well Labor Day, I mean I might play something, where, any particular place?

Oh yeah I played there but didn’t, other than, it wasn’t a Labor Day thing. I mean I played there something like at least two or three times a year and I’m supposed to play there — one year I didn’t play there because I was in New York pretty often. See my fellow that books me lives in New York and he’s got an apartment. Any time I want to stay around New York, I mean, it won’t cost me nothing, I mean my room and stuff like that because it’s his place. But other than that I couldn’t be around New York without working because hotel rooms are around a hundred dollars or better. You’ve got to be working or have something going to lay around New York.
